name: City Council Adjourned Regular Meeting of August 14, 2019
minutes_text:
APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL ADJOURNED REGULAR MEETING
  OF AUGUST 14, 2019

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:00 pm

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Jerry Velasco, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Velasco  5-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION (5:00 p.m. – 6:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 5:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 6:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 6:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 6:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

  Mayor Quintero invited members of the public to address the City Council on
  Closed Session Items 4.1 through 4.5.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at
  approximately 6:02 p.m.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 7:36 p.m.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at
  approximately 8:17 p.m.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 10:51 p.m.

  Assistant City Attorney Richard Padilla reported out of Closed Session with
  respect to Items 4.1 through 4.5.
   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 14, 2019

4.1  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.8 – Conference
  with Real Property Negotiator.

  Property Location:
  APN’S: 8532-014-001, 8532-014-002, 8532-014-007 and 8532-013-026, 8532-
  013-027, 8532-013-029

  Name of Party City is Negotiating with:
  289 North Robertson Blvd. II, LLC, a California Limited Liability Company

  City’s Designated Negotiators:
  Alex Hamilton, City Manager; Alma Martinez, Assistant City Manager; and Dave
  Gondek, Senior Deputy City Attorney

  Under Discussion:
  Discussion of both price and terms.

  General update, no final action

4.2  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 – Public
  Employee Discipline, Dismissal, and Release.

  The City Council approved the terms of a Settlement Agreement with
  incumbent City Manager Alex Hamilton the terms which are specified in the
  document which will be made available to the public open request. The
  salient points of the payout are his existing bank of vacation leave and sick
  leave $32,151.15 and $15,556.24, City to also provide Mr. Hamilton the
  balance of his deferred comp that he is entitled under his contract in the
  amount of $16,770.83, City will pay subject to reimbursement medical cobra
  benefits through January 31, 2020. Similar dental and vision cobra benefits
  through January 31, 2020. Should Mr. Hamilton obtain employment prior to
  January 31, 2020, the benefit would cease. Finally a supplemental
  consideration in exchange for a settlement and release of all claims of
  $60,000.

4.3  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6 – Conference
  with Labor Negotiator - Unrepresented Employee – Title: City Manager.

  Alma Martinez has been appointed City Manager and this will be subject to
  Council approval under Item 8.1 of the agenda at which time I will read out
  the salient deal points.

4.4  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 – Public
  Employee Appointment/Employment – Title: City Manager.

  General update, no final action

4.5  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6 – Conference
  with Labor Negotiator – Represented Employees.

  Bargaining Units Subject to Negotiations:
  El Monte Police Mid-Managers Association; and El Monte Police Officers
  Association.

  City’s Designated Negotiators:
  Alex Hamilton, City Manager; Alma Martinez, Assistant City Manager; and
  Kristen Enomoto, Sr. Management Analyst.

  General update, no final action

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Velasco  5-0

   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 14, 2019

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS
  (Commencing at 6:00 p.m. or as soon thereafter as the City Council reconvene from Closed
  Session/Short Recess)

5.  INVOCATION:  Mayor Quintero

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  Mayor Quintero

7.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
  deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
  agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
  Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
  Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
  instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
  of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
  proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
  public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
  of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
  threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
  interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
  must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
  religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
  marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

  Jane Myring – I am here for a specific reason you all ran knowing that you had an
  obligation to the City, to the citizens of the City and we have meetings on the first
  Tuesday and the third Tuesday of the month your citizens know this and they can put
  this on their calendar. It is very distressing when you come to a meeting and you do not
  have a quorum. You guys obligated to this I don’t care what your other things if you run
  for Council to run a City you should be here when you are supposed to be here.
  Because how do we know when you reschedule the meeting because this is how it is
  supposed to be. I think it is bad for the people who voted you in that you cannot be here
  at your appointed time.

  Mary Ann Powers – First FedEx in Arcadia is a problem in our City we have trucks
  running constantly up and down Roseglen no one seems to be able to stop it and if you
  contact the Arcadia Logistic Center it is extremely disrespectful for them to be flying the
  American flag that is nothing but tatters and according to the rules and regulations of
  flying a flying a flag you put a light on it if you are going to fly it at night. The next thing I

  3
   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 14, 2019

  want to talk about is we have time to talk about Lyft and Uber drivers but we don’t have
  time to talk about a sit down with the County and say wait a minute what are we going to
  do about this $1.9 million increase and how we can get rid of it we can’t afford it.
  Another thing all these special projects that everyone wants to have $30,000 a
  Councilmember for special projects. Special projects are wonderful but we are dipping
  into our reserves and that is an emergency fund and as lovely as it is to have the
  nutcracker here at Christmas time the citizens can watch it on PBS we can’t afford
  money for programs like that. I mean if we want to have a Christmas program in the City
  we have Thespians in the City. Why not get together with Parks & Recreation and have
  our children and our youth put on a beautiful day over at the El Monte High School
  auditorium that would be much better. Let’s look at our reserves as an emergency fund I
  don’t want to think that you are going to dip into your emergency fund to go hear a
  concert in downtown so don’t expect to do it with our City funds. We need to cut things to
  the bone and if you are still serving snacks for Council meetings and the citizens are
  paying for it that needs to stop.

  Cosme Jimenez – I want to respond to a comment made by Councilwoman Jessica
  Ancona because I belong to the Measure EM/GG Committee and we have been working
  with the Council as much as we can. We’ve worked with the helicopter program and
  bring it to the Council and we were able to save over a million dollars a year with the
  helicopter program alone. We are still working we tried several times with Fire Station
  167 on Peck Road and Bryant we can save about $2.5 million a year being that the
  union doesn’t want that station to be closed it becomes political incorrect to do it. I also
  have a report from the Fire Department when the station was closed in 2009/2010 for a
  year. The response time when it was open was 4.19 minutes when it was closed it was
  4.21 that tells you if we need the station or not. I am not saying we don’t need it I am
  saying when it is time to cut when it is time to save we need to do something. That
  station needs to be closed not because I said it because we need the money we are
  throwing money away.

8.  REGULAR AGENDA:

  8.1  Consideration and Possible Approval of City Manager Employment Agreement.

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:
  Pending Closed Session Discussion and Deliberation it is recommended that the
  City Council move to:

  1. Ratify City Manager appointment;
  2. Approve a written employment agreement to be made available to the public
  before consideration of this agenda item and the salient terms of which will be
  disclosed to the public before approval of this item; and
  3. Authorize the Mayor to execute the City Manager Employment Agreement on
  behalf of the City.

  Total Cost: N/A  Account No: N/A
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Mayor Pro Ten Velasco  5-0
  The base salary for the contract will be $220,000 per year the contract will
  have a term of three (3) years with the City Council option to extend for two
  (2) years. There will be tiered severance six (6) months after the first year,
  nine (9) months after the second year and twelve (12) months after the third
  year. Car allowance of $450, City contribution of the current maximum
  deposit into an IRS 457 Plan and consistent with the prior City Manager
  agreement there will be medical benefits consistent with the Executive
  Team, cellphone, term life insurance. Ms. Martinez is also a Pepra
  employee so she will be contributing fifty percent of her normal cost
  toward that all other terms will be stated in the agreement.

13.  ADJOURNMENT:

  With no objection Mayor Quintero adjourned the City Council meeting at 11:15
  p.m.

  The next Regular Meeting of the City Council will be held on August 20, 2019 at 6:00
  p.m. This Agenda will be posted on the City’s website, www.ci.el-monte.ca.us, and
  physically posted no less than 72 hours prior to the start of the subject regular meeting.
  Although it is the City’s practice and desire to electronically post a copy of this Agenda
  along with supporting material as part of its website posting, the size or formatting of
  certain supporting materials may render their website posting infeasible. Nevertheless,
  all supporting materials related to any item on this Agenda, that is made available to the
  members of the council may be inspected by members of the public at the City Clerk’s
  Office located at 11333 Valley Boulevard, El Monte, Monday through Thursday, 7:00 am
  – 5:30 pm. For more information, please call the City Clerk’s Office at 626-580-2016.

  All public meetings and events sponsored or conducted by the City of El Monte are held
  in sites accessible to persons with disabilities. Requests for accommodations may be
  made by calling the office of the City Clerk at (626) 580-2016 at least three (3) working
  days prior to the event, if possible. This Agenda and copies of documents distributed at
  the meeting are available in alternative formats upon request.
